newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire gains on chairman appointment.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire gains on chairman appointment.

text.p: Shares in chemicals group Yorkshire Group Plc rose on Monday after the company said it appointed Stuart Wallis, formerly chief executive of Fisons Plc, as its next chairman, replacing Phillip Lowe who is retiring.
The stock was up 14p at 255 by 0745 GMT.
"Anything that perks up the company's management has got to be good news," said one analyst, who asked not to be named, "and Wallis has a good reputation."
In a statement, Yorkshire group managing director Michael Greenhalgh said Wallis had a "proven track record in the development and implementation of global business strategies."
Wallis quit Fisons after the drug company was last year acquired by Rhone-Poulenc Rorer.

Last month Yorkshire reported a rise in first-half pre-tax profit to 6.9 million stg from 5.9 million a year before, but said trading conditions remained tough in all the markets in which it operates.
